_doc: A capital's or a city's own river through its streets on the land field (Brian, 18 November: the battle's ground matches the map; the design director, b526).

Keyed by the town's name as the game names it (townName). The hand list follows the real city in 1939 to 1945, not the campaign map's generalized courses; the historian checked it in one pass (18 November, historian-pass.md).

form: 'through' (the river runs through the city), 'meet' (two rivers meet at the city: join is the second, joinFrom the compass bearing from the meeting toward where it comes from), 'shore' (the river runs along one edge of the city, not through it: water is the compass bearing from the city's heart to it).
flows: the compass bearing, in degrees, the river flows toward as it passes the city's heart. great: wider than about 250 metres there (drawn wider).

Only rivers a street fight would meet: no covered or small streams, and no sea coasts (a bay, a harbour, a strait). Where the card prices a crossing (the province's river between the armies), that river is the field's and this list adds nothing.

bridges, joinBridges: the city's road bridges over its river and the second river in 1939 to 1945, as the historian counted them for the design director's b596 (bridges.md); 6 stands for six or more, 0 for none (ferries only). The field lays that many, those nearest the heart, and every other avenue ends at a quay; at six or more every avenue has its bridge.

strip: a shore city that runs along its water, long and shallow (the art director, 19 November): where its water lies behind the defence, its streets run the field's whole width along the bank and reach about 800 m inland. Marked by the design director (b617, b619) where the historian finds the city about 4 to 1 or more along its water with one heart on the bank: Stalingrad, Molotov, Tbilisi, Khabarovsk, Krasnoyarsk. A river through the city (Tbilisi, Krasnoyarsk) lies up or across, never behind as a shore, so there the mark is carried but not drawn.

Krakow.note: Wawel and the old town on the north bank, Podgorze south

Berlin.note: through Mitte; the Moltke bridge, April 1945

Hamburg.note: the old town on the north bank, the port islands and Harburg south

Cologne.note: the old town on the west bank, Deutz east

Stuttgart.note: the city's east edge; Bad Cannstatt across

Vienna.note: the inner city south-west of it, Floridsdorf across. The water at the inner city's north-east edge is the Danube Canal (about 50 m); the main stream runs about 2 km beyond it. The April 1945 fighting ran along the canal

Prague.note: the Old Town east, Mala Strana and the castle west

Lyon.note: the Presqu'ile between them, meeting at its southern tip

Bordeaux.note: the crescent; La Bastide on the right bank

Amsterdam.note: the IJ along the old centre's north edge, the station on its islands; the Amstel (70 to 100 m) came in from the south-east and stopped at the old centre. In a street fight the canal ring matters more

Rotterdam.note: the Willems bridge, May 1940; Feijenoord south

Liverpool.note: the estuary along the west; Birkenhead across

Riga.note: the old town on the east bank

Kaunas.note: the old town on the point where the Neris comes in

Turin.note: the centre west of it, the hill east

Bern.note: a horseshoe: the Aare wraps the old town on the north, east and south in a gorge 30 to 40 m down, open to the west; one edge, east, is the best single choice

Lisbon.note: the estuary along the city's south edge (b526: a shore, not through it)

Bratislava.note: the old town north, Petrzalka south

Belgrade.note: the old town and Kalemegdan on the point (b526)

Smolensk.note: the kremlin walls on the south bank

Kiev.note: the city on the high west bank, Darnitsa across (b526)

Moscow.note: the Kremlin on the north bank

Yaroslavl.note: the old town on the point (the Strelka)

Gorky.note: the upper town and kremlin over the point

Voronezh.note: the city on the west bank, the Left Bank across (July 1942)

Saratov.note: the city along the west bank, Engels across

Rostov.note: the city on the north bank, the flood plain south

Stalingrad.note: the city along the west bank, more than 20 km long and 2 to 5 km deep; no bridge in 1942

Tbilisi.note: 15 to 20 km along the Kura in its gorge, 3 to 5 deep, the old town and Metekhi on the banks (b619)

Cairo.note: the city on the east bank, Giza west, the islands between

Washington.note: along the city's south-west, Arlington across

Philadelphia.note: the Schuylkill through the west is smaller

New York.note: along Manhattan's west, flowing south; the East River is a tidal strait, left out

Boston.note: the basin between Boston and Cambridge

Pittsburgh.note: they meet at the Point to make the Ohio

Ottawa.note: Parliament Hill over it, Hull across

Ciudad Trujillo.note: the old city on its west bank

Osaka.note: the old course of the Yodo, round Nakanoshima

Hiroshima.note: the delta's channels; the Aioi bridge

Seoul.note: Keijo under Japan; south of the old city, by Yongsan

Nanking.note: the walls' north-west side by the river, Pukou across

Shanghai.note: the Bund on the west bank, Pudong across

Hankow.note: Hankow, Hanyang and Wuchang about the meeting

Chungking.note: the old city on the point

Khabarovsk.note: 12 to 15 km along the Amur's right bank, 3 to 4 deep, on the cliff with three ridges running down to the river (b619)

Ufa.note: the Ufa River comes into the Belaya at the city's northern edge

Molotov.note: Perm until 1940, Molotov from 1940 to 1957; the centre on the Kama's south-east bank; 20 to 25 km along it with Motovilikha, 3 to 4 deep (b619)

Kuibyshev.note: the Samara River comes into the Volga at the city's southern edge

Kazan.note: along the kremlin's north side, west into the Volga; the heart south of it, only suburbs across. The Volga ran 5 to 6 km off before its reservoir (1955-57)

Krasnoyarsk.note: 10 to 12 km along the Yenisei, 2 to 3 deep, between the river and the hills (b619)

Khartoum.note: the White Nile from the south, the Blue Nile from the east; the Nile runs north from the meeting. Khartoum on the Blue Nile's south bank at the point, Omdurman across the White Nile
